location: Always > Fail-fast ('a reaped child has appended a `fail` record'); Always > Child ('The child judges an engine's `fail` with `cell_state`')
issue: The spec never says which `fail` counts: the state written by `build_record`/`cell_state` (both `derive_state`), or the effective state readers use. `ps-plan-layers.record_state` reads a stored `pass`/`fail` as `inconclusive`, reason `incomplete-record`, when any INCOMPLETE_KEYS field is null (`authored_assertions`, `scenario_notes`, `inconclusive`, `browser_notes`, `install`, ...). `derive_state` ignores those keys. A child cell with findings but `authored_assertions: null` is therefore appended as `fail`, starts cross-version fail-fast, and makes the run exit 3. Plan and aggregate then read that same record as inconclusive. Inside the child, the same gap lets engine fail-fast mark the next engine `not-run` on a finding that is not conclusive.
implementation_impact: Queued versions are cancelled, and later engines skipped, on a record the gate itself calls inconclusive. This breaks the Design Notes rationale that only a conclusive finding triggers fail-fast. The `not-run` reasons then point at a cell whose plan reason is `inconclusive`, not `fail`.
suggestion: Define the trigger as the appended record's effective state (`record_state(rec)['state'] == 'fail'`). Have the child apply the INCOMPLETE_KEYS rule before engine fail-fast, or let `cell_state` apply it. Add a test: a child cell with findings and `authored_assertions: null` is appended as inconclusive/incomplete-record, or at least does not trigger fail-fast.

location: Always > Fail-fast ('A child exit 2 does the same with `input-error after <ver>`'); Tasks > docs ('`input-error after …` once the rejected input is fixed')
issue: Every child is launched as `uv run <script>` (`plan_children`). uv also returns exit code 2 for its own failures: dependency resolution or download failing offline, a cache or lock error, an interpreter that cannot be fetched. Those are infra failures, not a rejected input. The slice now turns any exit 2 into `not-run` records with reason `input-error after <ver>` in every queued cell's history. The docs being written tell the operator to fix 'the rejected input', and the interim companion ends the E2E loop for the whole session.
implementation_impact: A transient network or uv-cache failure on one child cancels every queued cell, writes misleading `input-error` evidence, and ends E2E for the session. Fixing it has no visible input to fix.
suggestion: Make the child mark a genuine input error before it exits 2: a sentinel line on stderr, or an `-o` payload `{status: 'input-error'}` written before exit. ps-run-layer then treats an exit 2 without that marker as `crash` (no fail-fast). This changes the contract rule 'a child exit 2', so put it under Ask First. Otherwise state the limitation in the docs task and log it in deferred-work.

location: Design Notes > Admission ('START wait-slots, then the ALIVE wait-slots heartbeat'); Tasks > ps-flashlight-run.py (wait-phase helper)
issue: The `wait-slots` heartbeat runs on a background thread, like `fl.phase`, while the admission loop runs on the main thread. If the loop stalls, the thread keeps writing `ALIVE wait-slots` every 15 s. Ways it can stall: blocked on `slots.lock` held by a SIGSTOPped run, a hung registry read, or an exception swallowed in a worker. The wait itself has no bound: an own-queue wait is unbounded by contract, and `wait-slots` is never `SLOW`. That leaves the silent-log rule ('no new line ±3 min without DONE') as the only hang detector in run-phases.md and headless.md, and the heartbeat defeats it.
implementation_impact: A wedged ps-run-layer looks healthy forever. Interactive monitoring never reports it, headless never stops it, and the session hangs with no signal.
suggestion: Write the heartbeat from the loop thread at the end of each pass, or put the age of the last completed pass in the ALIVE detail (e.g. `last pass 4s ago`). Then the docs can state 'ALIVE wait-slots whose last pass is older than N×SLOT_POLL = stuck'. Add a test with a stubbed pass that blocks: the log goes silent or shows a growing pass age.

location: Design Notes > Records ('When ps-run-layer exits, a log it truncated that lacks `DONE` gets one ... `rc=stopped` on a stop, else `rc=<run exit code>`')
issue: The DONE rule covers only a normal return and a `--stop-job` stop. ps-run-layer is not wrapped in `run_main_with_progress`, so an uncaught exception or KeyboardInterrupt (Ctrl-C) during admission has no run exit code. Examples: a bug in the admission loop, `cleanup_orphans` raising, an OSError on the lock dir. Every queued version's log is left with `START wait-slots` and ALIVE lines but no `END wait-slots` and no `DONE`. The heartbeat threads are daemon threads and die mid-line. The children have the `rc=crash` guarantee; the logs ps-run-layer now owns do not.
implementation_impact: After a ps-run-layer crash, monitors see open phases with no DONE. Headless applies the silent-log rule, `--stop-job`s a job that is already dead, and returns `blocked` with a misleading reason. Interactive runs report a 'suspected hang' rather than a crash.
suggestion: Specify a `try/except BaseException` around the E2E run: close every open wait (`END wait-slots error(<Exc>)`) and write `DONE rc=crash` to each truncated log that lacks DONE and has no running child, then re-raise. On KeyboardInterrupt write `rc=stopped`. Add a test where a stubbed `daemon_slot_usage` raises.

location: Design Notes > Admission ('A `psm.slots` label or claim `cost` that is not an integer ≥ 1 counts 1, shown as `=?`'; tokens `<psm.job>@<host>=<cost>`)
issue: Only values below 1 or non-integer values are defined. A labelled container with `psm.slots=100000` (a typo, a script bug, or deliberate) is counted at face value and fills every run's cap on the daemon. Every run then ends in `no-slots`, with no upper bound or clamp. The `psm.job` and `psm.owner-host` label values are copied verbatim into ALIVE lines, `errors` and the no-slots record, but they are not validated. A value containing a tab or newline breaks the tab-separated `docker ps --format` parsing. A newline can also inject a forged line, such as a fake `DONE rc=0`, into another run's progress log. `_list_artifacts` documents exactly this label-forgery concern.
implementation_impact: One bad label denies E2E to every session on the daemon. Progress logs and history `errors` can carry injected content that monitors parse as tokens.
suggestion: Clamp a counted cost to a sane maximum, e.g. `len(SUPPORTED_ENGINES)`, and treat anything above it as `=?`, cost 1 or the clamp. Validate `psm.job` with `valid_job_id` and the host against a hostname charset, and replace anything else with `?`. Parse with a delimiter-safe format such as `{{json .Labels}}` per line. Add tests for a huge cost and for a label containing a newline or tab.

location: Design Notes > Admission ('spawning each admitted version at once (claim written first)'); Design Notes > Claims ('removed when its child is reaped')
issue: The claim is added before spawn and removed only 'when its child is reaped'. The spec does not cover a spawn that fails: Popen raising OSError/ENOMEM, `uv` missing from PATH, a thread pool that cannot start a worker. In that case there is no child to reap. Today a runner exception becomes `rc=None` (crash) only because `_spawn` runs inside a pool future. The new loop 'spawns each admitted version at once' and need not keep that shape. The wait-slots outcome for such a version (`ok` was already written) and its DONE line are also unspecified.
implementation_impact: A phantom own claim is held for the rest of the run. With `--slots 1` it blocks every later version until the no-slots clock expires. Or the exception escapes the loop and kills the run with claims still in the registry file until atexit.
suggestion: State that a failed spawn is handled like a reaped child with no output: claim removed under `slots.lock`, `crash` records for its cells, no fail-fast, and `DONE rc=crash` in its log. Add a test with a runner that raises on the second spawn under `--slots 1`.

location: Design Notes > Interim cost/mode ('every version is admitted at cost 1 with `--sequential-browsers`, so ... engine fail-fast always applies under ps-run-layer')
issue: In the contract, engine fail-fast is part of the sequential fallback, which applies only when there are too few slots for parallel browsers. This slice makes it unconditional for every ps-run-layer run, including a lone Phase 1 run `--cells V:chromium+firefox` on an idle daemon. Today that run drives both engines in one boot and reports Firefox-specific failures too. After this slice a Chromium `fail` leaves Firefox `not-run`, so Firefox-only defects surface only on a later cold boot. That adds fix-loop iterations, each a full cold boot, which is the wait the SPEC exists to cut. The spec states the decision but does not weigh this cost, and it is not among the decisions already taken.
implementation_impact: There are more cold boots per convergence in Phase 1 until CAP-7 lands. Under the interim, CAP-3's time saving can turn negative for two-browser versions.
suggestion: Either justify the trade-off explicitly (why losing the second engine's findings is acceptable before CAP-7), or pass `--sequential-browsers` only when the version is not alone in the run or a free-slot check says parallel would not fit. The child-side fallback tests (SPEC CAP-3 success) do not depend on ps-run-layer always passing the flag.

location: Design Notes > Admission ('The `no-slots` clock is one run-wide accumulator ... its limit is the contract's startup timeout')
issue: The clock source is not specified. If the accumulator adds wall-clock deltas (`time.time()`), a WSL2 host sleep or hibernate, or the known WSL clock resync jump after resume, advances it by hours in one pass. Every still-queued cell then gets `no-slots` immediately on resume. The `phase` helper uses `time.monotonic`, but nothing requires the accumulator to.
implementation_impact: After a laptop sleep, spurious `no-slots` records appear and the run exits 1 even though the cap freed up. This is especially likely in the long own-queue waits this slice introduces.
suggestion: Require `time.monotonic()` for the accumulator and the `wait-slots` seconds. Optionally cap one pass's contribution at about SLOT_POLL plus the count timeout, so one long suspended pass cannot exhaust the limit on its own.

location: Design Notes > Admission ('`ALIVE` details join the same tokens with `, `'); Tasks > docs (wait-slots meaning)
issue: The ALIVE detail lists what fills the cap but not which kind of wait is running. A version queued behind its own run's children waits without limit. A version blocked only by others is on the bounded `no-slots` clock. The line shows neither the mode nor the accumulator's value and limit. Own claims and foreign tokens look alike apart from the job id, and `_budget()` shows only the phase's elapsed time, which keeps growing during the unbounded own-queue wait.
implementation_impact: An operator or headless monitor cannot tell a normal own-queue wait from one about to end in `no-slots`. They cannot decide whether to free slots now or keep waiting, which the docs task tells them to do for `no-slots`.
suggestion: Add a fixed suffix to the ALIVE detail, e.g. `own-queue` versus `no-slots in <limit-acc>s`. Document it in run-phases.md next to 'wait-slots never SLOW'. Assert it in the Own queue and Foreign full tests.

location: Tasks > docs (headless.md: only the automatic `--cleanup-orphans` exception)
issue: This slice adds two new ways for headless runs to lose E2E evidence. `no-slots`: a busy daemon now ends cells after 180 s, where today the run simply booted. `not-run`: cells left unstarted after another version's failure. The headless return carries only `ready`, `pass`, `e2e_conclusive`, `layers_run`. The `not_run_cells` and per-version `reason` return fields are a deferred Headless bullet. headless.md tells callers that `ready: false` without Docker or a browser is an environment fact. So a caller such as psm-develop cannot tell 'daemon busy, retry later' from 'Docker missing' or a module defect, and the docs task does not change headless.md or the callers to say so.
implementation_impact: Headless callers may misreport a busy shared daemon as a missing environment, or loop without useful action. Nothing in their docs mentions `no-slots`.
suggestion: Extend the headless.md docs item: a run whose cells end `no-slots` returns `complete`, `ready: false`, and the caller should report 'Docker daemon at its slot cap (psm_e2e_slots)' and suggest retrying. Add an `e2e_infra_reason` (or similar) one-liner to the return, or log a deferred-work entry that pins this to the CAP-1 Headless bullet.
